claims.claim: Integral switching flows are exactly feasible points of an affine binary-parity lattice system.
claims.evidence: For an integral flow the even-minus-odd imbalance is an integer in [0,1], hence ε_v∈{0,1}; putting p_v equal to the odd-edge flow gives the two outgoing flows p_v+ε_v and p_v. Substitution into outflow-minus-inflow conservation gives (2I−A^T)p=δ_o+((A^0)^T−I)ε exactly, and the substitution reverses. The internal uniform-walk matrix is transient because every nonterminal has a sink path, so 2I−A^T is nonsingular. Adjugate divisibility is therefore equivalent to integral p. Summed conservation gives nonnegative integral terminal inflows totaling one.
claims.witness: The mutually inverse maps are p_v=x(v,s_1(v)), ε_v=x(v,s_0(v))−x(v,s_1(v)) and x(v,s_0(v))=p_v+ε_v, x(v,s_1(v))=p_v.
claims.search_method: Independent algebraic derivation from the authorized source definitions, including conservation, transience, and terminal cancellation; no external search.

claims.claim: At fixed positive-level width r, the affine system is block lower-Hessenberg and gives an exact reduction of ARRIVAL, but it retains N binary choices.
claims.evidence: For an edge from L_j to L_i, the shortest-path triangle inequality gives j≤i+1. Thus, after level ordering, row block i has no nonzero column block beyond i+1 in either matrix, exactly the block lower-Hessenberg condition. Claim 0 and the source certificate theorem establish equivalence between b_1=1 feasibility and a YES ARRIVAL instance. There are N explicitly represented parity bits; fixing them leaves one exact rational linear solve and polynomial-bit arithmetic. Arbitrarily long backward edges appear arbitrarily far below the diagonal, so no bounded-band conclusion is asserted.
claims.witness: The reduction maps an ARRIVAL instance to M,H,δ_o and the affine terminal form b_1, with ε∈{0,1}^N and p∈Z_{≥0}^N; the inverse map is the edge-flow construction from claim 0.
claims.search_method: Checked the edge-level quantifier in both matrix orientations and independently applied the authorized source certificate theorem.

claims.claim: Width three admits at least 2^(N/3) distinct feasible parity vectors with the same terminal signature, even when every vertex is reachable from the origin.
claims.evidence: The displayed graph has exactly three vertices at each positive level: every vertex has a predecessor-level edge and no edge decreases distance by more than one. From c_k, the c-rail reaches every c_i, and c_i→a_i→b_i reaches the other two vertices. For each subset S, the c-rail carries one unit to sink 1 and each selected a_i↔b_i even-edge pair is a unit circulation. Direct conservation gives supply only at c_k, every imbalance is 0 or 1, and terminal inflow is always (0,1). The selected levels are recoverable from the parity vector, yielding 2^k=2^(N/3) distinct vectors.
claims.witness: For S⊆{1,…,k}, set x(c_i,c_{i−1})=1 for all i and x(a_i,b_i)=x(b_i,a_i)=1 exactly for i∈S, with every other edge flow zero.
claims.search_method: Proved the level and reachability properties symbolically, then exhaustively checked all 2^k subsets for k=1,…,8 with integer arithmetic.

claims.claim: Exact harmonic duality gives a polynomial bound on fixed-width boundary signatures.
claims.evidence: For z=y−x with common supply, summing Σ_e z_e(h_t(tail)−h_t(head)) by vertices gives x^−(t)−y^−(t), while summing the two outgoing arcs at each vertex gives Σ_v(d_y(v)−d_x(v))g_t(v). Since both imbalances lie in [0,1] and |g_t(v)|≤1/2, every coordinate diameter is at most N/2. Fixed total terminal inflow makes the last coordinate dependent, so at most (floor(N/2)+1)^(r−1) integral signatures occur for fixed supply and fixed r. The claimed exact attainability for φ≡1 follows by solving the stated transient affine system for total outflows; monotone iteration from total outflow one preserves nonnegativity and converges.
claims.witness: Choose d_y(v)=1,d_x(v)=0 where g_t(v)>0 and reverse these choices where g_t(v)<0. The φ≡1 construction realizes both imbalance vectors and makes the terminal-coordinate difference Σ_v|g_t(v)|.
claims.search_method: Re-derived directed summation by parts without identifying antiparallel arcs, proved the counting bound, and exact-checked the attainability identity on the rail families.

claims.claim: For fixed terminal count and fixed integral supply, all integral terminal-inflow signatures admitted by the fractional switching-flow polyhedron can be enumerated in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: The feasible region and terminal forms are rational linear systems. For each of r−1 coordinates, LP computes finite extrema whose difference is at most N/2 by claim 3, so its interval contains at most floor(N/2)+1 integers. Enumerating the Cartesian product is polynomial for fixed r; fixed total supply determines the last coordinate. An equality-constrained LP accepts exactly those candidate signatures realized by fractional switching flows. This proves both output soundness and completeness and does not purport to enforce internal integrality.
claims.witness: The enumeration consists of integer tuples in the first r−1 LP ranges, followed by b_r=Σ_vφ(v)−Σ_{t<r}b_t and one feasibility LP per tuple.
claims.search_method: Checked range cardinalities, total-flow conservation, LP feasibility equivalence, output size, and bit-complexity from first principles.

claims.claim: A general range bound survives at arbitrary level width, but it can grow linearly with the number of levels.
claims.evidence: An absorbing walk starting at level at least i must hit L_{i−1}, since one edge cannot reduce shortest-path distance by more than one. Strong Markov therefore puts every such hitting probability in [m_{i−1},M_{i−1}], proving nested ranges. Both successors of v∈L_i lie at level at least i−1, so |g(v)|≤W_{i−1}/2; summing r vertices per level gives the stated bound. Claim 7 supplies a family where the resulting gap mass is Θ(k), establishing that linear growth actually occurs.
claims.witness: The three-rail family has W_i=1−i/(k+1) and exact total gap mass k(k+7)/(4(k+1)), which is linear in the number k of positive levels.
claims.search_method: Proved the first-hitting range inclusion symbolically and exact-checked the linear-growth witness for multiple depths.

claims.claim: At the one-positive-level boundary, the exact maximum gap mass is r/2; therefore the width-two stability constant fails at width three in the smallest possible depth.
claims.evidence: Harmonicity gives |g(v)|=|h(s_0(v))−h(s_1(v))|/2≤1/2, so r vertices give the universal upper bound r/2. Sending each vertex directly to different sinks attains equality. With supply one per vertex, flows (1/2,1/2) and (1,0) are feasible and differ in sink-1 inflow by r/2, making the diameter exact. At r=3 this is 3/2>1, and one positive level is the least nonempty depth.
claims.witness: Use s_0(v)=0 and s_1(v)=1 for all r vertices, x_v=(1/2,1/2), and y_v=(1,0).
claims.search_method: Applied the pointwise harmonic bound and exact-checked the construction and both flow systems for r=1,…,9.

claims.claim: For every fixed r≥3, harmonic gap mass and same-supply fractional switching-flow diameter can be Θ(N), so the universal N/2 bound is asymptotically order-tight up to an r-dependent constant.
claims.evidence: Direct substitution verifies h(a_i)=i/(2(k+1)), h(b_i)=1−i/(2(k+1)), and h(c_i)=1/2. Summing exact gaps gives k(k+7)/(4(k+1)) for r=3. Each added centered vertex has value 1/2 and the same level-i gap as c_i, yielding k[4+(r−2)(k+3)]/[4(k+1)]. With N=rk and fixed r≥3 this is Θ(N). Claim 3's φ≡1 endpoint construction realizes the entire gap as a difference of two same-supply fractional flows.
claims.witness: For each vertex choose the two endpoint imbalances according to the sign of g(v); exact conservation solutions with φ(v)=1 then have sink-inflow difference equal to the displayed gap sum.
claims.search_method: Solved all harmonic systems and both endpoint-flow systems using exact fractions for k=2,…,8 and r=3,…,7, while also checking the claimed levelsets.

claims.claim: Within-level hitting-probability order is not locally determined at width three, and two positive levels already suffice for this failure.
claims.evidence: Both completions have exactly L_1={a,b,c} and L_2={X,Y,Z}, satisfy the binary simple-graph conditions, and agree on all outgoing edges from L_1. Exact harmonic solutions give (h(a),h(b))=(3/22,1/22) in completion A and (1/22,3/22) in completion B. Thus identical preceding-level data and identical current-level outgoing data yield opposite a,b orders. The witness uses only two positive levels.
claims.witness: Completion A uses X→(c,b),Y→(a,b); completion B uses X→(a,b),Y→(c,a), with the common edges stated in the draft.
claims.search_method: Constructed both transition systems, recomputed shortest-path levels, and solved both harmonic systems by exact Gaussian elimination.
